newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Tobacco profits down, jobs cut.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Tobacco profits down, jobs cut.

text.p: Jordan Tobacco and Cigarettes Company announced plans to cut jobs on Wednesday after reporting 1996 losses of 2.5 million dinars ($3.5 million), its first loss in 65 years of operation.
The company said in a statement it registered a profit of 596,471 dinars in 1995.
"We began downsizing our staff levels earlier this year," it said after Wednesday's annual general meeting. It did not say how many jobs would be lost in total.
The company said it would also move its headquarters into its factory premises in another attempt to cut costs.

It blamed punitive taxes, equal to 80 percent of the retail price, and a surge in the smuggling of cigarettes into Jordan as the main reason for fall in sales to 75.5 million dinars last year from 95.5 million in 1995.
Jordan's state investment arm said in February it was seeking bids from investors to buy its 40,000 shares in Jordan Tobacco, equivalent to 13.3 percent of the company's equity.
But the offer failed to spark much interest on the Amman bourse in the rarely-traded stock. Shares in Jordan Tobacco and Cigarettes last changed hands on April 8.
"It doesn't have a big capital and there isn't much of a float (of shares)," one broker said.
